cards.text: Isaiah 60 just promised Zion a sunrise, with the LORD as her everlasting light (Isaiah 60:19). Now Isaiah 61 opens with a voice that doesn't give its name: "The Spirit of the Lord GOD is on Me, because the LORD has anointed Me…" Anointed, friend, and that means there's a job to do.

cards.question: First job: the LORD has anointed this speaker to preach good news to the ___.

cards.text: The LORD has sent this speaker with a whole to-do list, and the brokenhearted are next on it. Friend, my to-do list is three words long, preheat the oven, and I STILL forget it.

cards.question: Next on the list are the brokenhearted. What is the speaker sent to do for them?
True or false: the speaker is also sent to proclaim freedom to the prisoners.

cards.text: The speaker is also sent to proclaim the year of the LORD's favor. A whole YEAR, friend, and back when I was stuck in a junk drawer, I'd have thrown a party for one good MINUTE.

cards.question: True or false: right next to the year of the LORD's favor, the speaker also proclaims a day of our God's vengeance.
The list keeps going. For all who mourn, the speaker is sent to ___ them.

cards.text: Then come three swaps for the mourners in Zion, with ashes, mourning and a spirit of despair all on the way out. I know swaps, friend, because I once got swapped out for a shiny new cookie stamper, so I'm rooting for these to go better than mine did.

cards.question: Instead of ashes, what does the speaker give the mourners in Zion?
Instead of mourning, the mourners in Zion get the oil of ___.
True or false: in place of a spirit of despair, the mourners in Zion get a garment of sackcloth.

cards.text: These mourners get a new name, and it comes with a picture of something the LORD Himself planted. Friend, the only thing I've ever grown is this mustache, and it's doing GREAT.

cards.question: What will the comforted mourners in Zion be called?
The LORD plants these oaks of righteousness. Why?

answers.text: So they may rule the nations

cards.text: OAKS, friend, not some little houseplant wilting on a windowsill. And these oaks of righteousness have a job waiting for them, a whole lot of ruins.

cards.question: What will the oaks of righteousness do with those ruins?

cards.text: Ruins from many generations get rebuilt, and strangers stand and feed the flocks while foreigners plow the fields and tend the vines. Friend, I had to send out invitations to get bakers in here, and these folks get help that just SHOWS UP.

cards.question: With others tending the flocks and fields, what will God's people be called?
True or false: with foreigners working their fields, God's people will feed on the wealth of nations.

cards.text: Now shame and humiliation get shown the door. Trust me, friend, nobody knows shame like a stamper who got slid to the back of a junk drawer behind a takeout menu.

cards.question: Instead of shame, God's people will have a double ___.

cards.text: A double portion in their land, and everlasting joy on top of it. Friend, when a cookie comes out with ONE extra chocolate chip I lose my mind, so a DOUBLE portion would have me face down in the sprinkles.
Then the LORD Himself speaks, and He gets straight to what He loves and what He hates.

cards.question: The LORD says He hates robbery and iniquity. What does He say He loves?

cards.text: In His faithfulness, the LORD says He will give His people their recompense and make an everlasting covenant with them. And the promise reaches all the way to their descendants.

cards.question: True or false: the descendants of God's people will stay unknown among the nations.
What will all who see these descendants acknowledge?

cards.text: Then the passage says, "I will rejoice greatly in the LORD, my soul will exult in my God…" That's not a polite golf clap, friend, that's hop-around-the-bakery joy.

cards.question: The passage says, "I will rejoice greatly in the LORD…" What reason does it give?

answers.text: God has clothed me with salvation
God has given me a long life
God has made me a great king

cards.text: The one rejoicing is also wrapped in a robe of righteousness, dressed like someone getting ready for one of the biggest days of their life. Me, I wear the same apron every single day, and I STILL look this good.

cards.question: Being wrapped in a robe of righteousness is like what?

answers.text: A bridegroom and a bride dressed up
A king dressed for his crowning

cards.text: A bride getting ready hits home in my bakery, because the Lamb's bride "has made herself ready." (Revelation 19:7) Then comes the last picture in Isaiah 61: a garden, where the earth brings forth its growth and seed springs up.

cards.question: As a garden makes seed spring up, the Lord GOD will cause ___ and praise to spring up before all the nations.
